extracted.intended_audience: authors, publishers, and others preparing submissions for the National Book Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural notes for submitting books to, and being evaluated by, the National Book Awards, including categories, judges, eligibility/submission process, and post-selection rights/medallions. Focused on titles published in the U.S. each year for consideration by the Awards' panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award categories (eligible genres)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Awards currently honor the best Fiction, Nonfiction, Poetry, Translated Literature, and Young People’s Literature, published each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the categories in which titles are reviewed and recognized by the National Book Awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging and selection process
rubrics_metrics.description: Twenty-five judges in five categories will review submitted titles and select the five Winners of the 76th National Book Awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges are organized by category (five per category) and are responsible for reviewing submitted titles and choosing winners; (further procedural details are available via the '2025 National Book Awards Judges' and related pages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and submission requirements (existence of formal rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility, the submission process, guidelines, and FAQs are provided for 2025 Submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page points to formal eligibility rules and submission guidelines that govern which titles may be entered and how; specific eligibility criteria and procedural requirements must be consulted on the linked submissions/guidelines page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose/mission informing evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Book Awards were established to celebrate the best writing in America and, per the Foundation's mission, to expand its audience and enhance the cultural value of great writing in America.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mission statement frames the Awards' evaluative intent—recognition is aimed at works considered 'the best writing in America' and at promoting cultural value and audience expansion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medallions and digital image rights availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Medallions and digital image rights are available for NBA Winner, Finalist, and Longlist titles; medallions are also offered for 5 Under 35 honorees and Distinguished Contribution to American Letters medalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medallions can be used on future or backlist titles (Winner/Finalist/Longlist distinctions noted); this is a post-selection procedural/right that affects how selected titles may market their recognition.
